root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Tarrasch Defense, Pseudo-Tarrasch

overview: Black hits the centre with ...c5 before White has played Nc3. White usually plays 4.cxd5 exd5 5.g3, fianchettoing, or 4.e3 Nf6 for a Meran-style position. Black gets an isolated queen's pawn or hanging pawns in exchange for active pieces, while White aims to blockade and use the extra space. It is more flexible than the main Tarrasch, with fewer forcing lines.

white_ideas.idea: g3, Bg2, O-O and dxc5 to leave Black with an isolated d-pawn
Blockade d4 and use the outpost on d4, trading pieces to emphasise the weak d5 pawn

black_ideas.idea: Active pieces with ...Nc6, ...Nf6, ...Be7 and ...O-O, using the IQP for attack
Exchange on d4 to get hanging pawns, then push ...d4 or ...c4

typical_structures.structure: Tarrasch isolated queen's pawn after cxd5 exd5 and dxc5 or ...cxd4
Hanging pawns on c5 and d5

character.notes: Positional, typical IQP middlegame; sound for both, strategic rather than tactical.

structure.notes: Symmetrical/IQP structure with half-open files and open diagonals: semi-open.

level.notes: IQP play needs strategic judgement but little memory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Pseudo-Tarrasch: 4.e3
sublines_that_differ.how: White keeps tension, a Meran/QGD-like position.

character.reason: Active IQP positions: neither forcing nor a fortress.

structure.reason: Symmetrical IQP exchange structure with an open c-file and diagonals.

plans.reason: Black accepts IQP or hanging pawns for activity.
